title: Subjective vs objective certainty
source_text: II. Porro docendi causa certitudo distingui potest in subjectivam atque objectivam. Certitudinem subjectivam voco, quam assensus quislibet actu in mente alicujus obtinet. Objectiva vero certitudo dicitur, quae per se cuilibet assensui debetur: seu, quae ratione habita objecti, menti inesse debet: & quam objectum, ut sic dicatur, jure suo a mente exigit.
pass_a_gloss: Further, for the sake of teaching, certainty can be distinguished into subjective and objective. I call subjective certainty that which any assent actually obtains in someone’s mind. But objective certainty is said to be that which of itself is owed to any assent: or, which, regard being had to the object, ought to be in the mind: and which the object, so to speak, by its own right exacts from the mind.
pass_b_english: Subjective = assent as it actually sits in a mind.
Objective = what the object of itself deserves / exacts from the mind.

lemmas.latin: quam objectum … jure suo a mente exigit
lemmas.gloss: which the object … by its own right exacts from the mind

choices.term: Certitudinem subjectivam voco, quam assensus quislibet actu in mente alicujus obtinet

rejected: subjective certainty means the object’s own right over the mind
